newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares trade at day's lows near close.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares trade at day's lows near close.

text.p: ** (0930 GMT) - Shares at Bombay exchanges slump in late
afternoon after weak start, speculator-led activity
** Bombay's top 30-share index falls 102.97 points, or 2.71
percent, to 3,692.20, off 3,791.34--intra-day high
** Lull in foreign fund activity, financial year-end
compulsions affect market--traders
** Buying support seen around 3,600-3,650 levels-traders
** National Stock Exchange 50-stock index down 10.65 points
or 1.0 percent, to 1,053.70
Blue chips at Bombay exchanges were traded near the day's lowest levels on Wednesday as lack of buying support from speculators put pressure on the market, dealers said.
"Long positions are getting liquidated. The slump is probably due to an absence of major buying interest by foreign funds," said Sanjeev Sanghvi, chief dealer at James Capel B&K.
The financial year-ending March 31, 1996 for companies acted as a dampener for making fresh investment before firms close their books, dealers said.
"People are trying to clean up their balance sheets. Some big players are lying low," said a local dealer.
"To an extent, there is some bit of money tightening also. I think the entire market is just happier marked at lower levels," said Capel's Sanghvi.
High monthly carry-forward charges of about 3.5 percent discouraged fresh speculative buying, traders said.
"The sharp charges are pulling down the market," the local dealer said.
The lower price levels in the market, are however likely to bring about some fund buying in pivotal stocks, dealers said.
A 16 percent rally in Bombay shares after a market-friendly 1997 budget came largely on the back of increased speculative buying with major funds missing the rally, they said.
Shares of Bayer India fell 50.0 rupees to 2,000 rupees at the Bombay exchange, with 30 shares traded near close.

The company said on Wednesday its net profit in calendar 1996 rose 158 percent to 103 million rupees against a comparitive net profit of 30.0 million rupes for the nine months ending December 31, 1996.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
